To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) The 6-OHDA rat model is a valid model for the human disease.

1. The dopamine transporter is a key target for the development of new imaging agents, as it can be used for both in vitro and in vivo imaging of the presynaptic dopamine nerve terminals in the striatum.

the 6-OHDA lesion model is a valid model for Parkinson's disease in that it reproduces the main features of the disease, i.e. the loss of dopamine in the striatum and the degeneration of dopaminergic neurons, as well as a number of clinical symptoms such as motor deficits, tremor, rigidity, and akinesia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new generation of radioligands which will be suitable for in vivo imaging of neurotransmitter systems.
the development and validation of in vivo imaging techniques for the study of neurotransmitter function in small animals.
the study of the effects of neuroleptics on the dopaminergic and serotonergic system in the rat 7-OHDA model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the rat 6-OHDA model of Parkinson's is a good model to study the effects of drugs on the nigro-striatal dopaminergic system, but that the results of such experiments cannot always be directly extrapolated to the clinical situation.
the 6-OHDA model is a valid model for human Parkinson's Disease, but that the model is limited in its ability to predict all the features of the disease in man, especially the non-motor symptoms.

the rat 6-OHDA model of Parkinson's Disease is a valid model to study neurotoxicity of the nigrostriatal dopaminergic system, and that it has predictive value in the sense that findings in this model are in line with findings in Parkinsonian patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, although there are similarities between the 6-OHDA model and the human condition, the model is not a perfect replica.
the 6-OHDA rat model is a good tool for the in vivo investigation of dopaminergic and serotonergic neurotransmitter function in Parkinson's disease.
the 6-OHDA model is a valid model for studying the effects of neurotoxins in vivo in small animals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in the 6-OHDA model of Parkinson's, the dopaminergic neurons are not completely destroyed.
the rat 6-OHDA model is a good translational model to study neurotransmitter function in Parkinson's disease.
